chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Urama, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Ibn Muskan, from one of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A Prophet from the Prophets of the Children of Israel passed by a man, part of him was under a wall and part of him was outside from it, the birds had dishevelled him and the dogs had ripped him apart. Then he continued and a city was raised for him, so he entered it, and there he was with a great one from its great ones, dead upon a bed decorated with brocade, with the incense burner around him.

So he said: 'O Lord! I testify that You are a Just Judge, not a tyrant. This servant of Yours did not associate with You even for the blink of an eye, yet You caused him to die with that death; and this is Your servant who did not believe in You even for the blink of an eye, yet You caused him to die with this death.'

So He said: 'My servant! I am as you said, a Just Judge not being tyrannous. That servant of Mine had an evil deed or a sin with Me, so I caused him to die with that death so that he would meet Me and nothing would remain upon him; and this servant of Mine had a good deed with Me, so I caused him to die with this death so that he would meet Me and there would not be a good deed for him with Me.'
ai.seo_question: How does divine justice explain why a righteous person might suffer a bad death while a sinner enjoys a good death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia concept of *Tajrid al-Amal* (stripping of deeds) through divine wisdom, where physical death serves as a mechanism to expiate specific sins or good deeds. It highlights that God’s justice is not merely retributive but also merciful, using death to clear the spiritual ledger so the soul meets its Creator with a clean slate. This narrative underscores the importance of continuous self-accountability, as even minor transgressions or virtues can be nullified by the finality of death.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bi Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Awrama, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, from Ibn Muskan, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A Prophet<sup>as</sup> from the Prophets<sup>as</sup> of the Children of Israel passed by a man, part of him was (crushed) under a wall and part of him was outside from it, the birds having had dishevelled him and the dogs having had ripped him apart. Then he<sup>as</sup> continued and came up to a city. So he entered it and there he was with a great one from its great ones (a VIP) having died upon a bed decorated with the brocade and incence was being burnt around him.

So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! I testify that You<sup>azwj</sup> are a Just Judge, not a tyrant. This servant of Yours<sup>azwj</sup> did not associate with You<sup>azwj</sup> even for the blink of an eye, (yet) You<sup>azwj</sup> Caused him to die with that death (crushed under the wall), and this is Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant who did not believe in You<sup>azwj</sup> even for the blink of an eye, (yet) You<sup>azwj</sup> Caused him to die with this death (on a decorated bed)’.

So He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: ‘My<sup>azwj</sup> servant! I<sup>azwj</sup> am like what you<sup>as</sup> said, a Just Judge not being tyrannous. That servant of Mine<sup>azwj</sup> had (committed) an evil deed in My<sup>azwj</sup> Presence, or a sin, (so) I<sup>azwj</sup> Caused him to die with that death (crushed under the wall) so that he would meet Me<sup>azwj</sup> and there would not remain anything upon him (to be Punished for); and this servant had a good deed for him in My<sup>azwj</sup> Presence, so I<sup>azwj</sup> Caused him to dies by this death (on a decorated bed) so that he would meet Me<sup>azwj</sup> and there would not be a single good deed for him in My<sup>azwj</sup> Presence’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Uramah from Nadr ibn Suwayd from Drust ibn abu Mansur from ibn Muskan from certain individuals of our people from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“A prophet of the prophets among the descendents of Israel once passed by a man. Half of the body of the man was under the wall and the other half out of the wall. The birds had scattered it and dogs had chewed it up. Then he came to a city where the chief had passed away. His body laid in state covered with the most beautiful cloths with a huge crowed around it.

He prayed to Allah saying, ‘O Lord, I testify that you make just decisions, and do not do injustice. That servant of Your’s never considered anything as your partner, even for a blinking of an eye, and You caused him to die that kind of death. This servant of You has not believed in You, even for a blinking of an eye, and You have caused him to die this kind of death.’

Allah said, ‘My servant, I am as you said I am. I make decisions with justice and do not do injustice. That servant of Mine had certain sins and I caused him to die that way so he could come in My presence without any sins. This servant of Mine had certain good deeds before Me, thus, I caused him to die this way so he would come in My presence without any good deeds before Me.’”
